brief.topic: A Root Found by Keeping One Promise

s01: We want the number whose cube is two.
At one, the cube is too small. At two, it is too large.
Keep a bracket with opposite signs for x cubed minus two.
Because the curve is continuous, it must cross zero between them.
Test the middle, one point five. Its cube is too large, so keep the left half.
The next middle is one point two five. Its cube is too small. Keep the right half.
Two more tests narrow the bracket further.
Each test preserves a root inside while cutting the interval width in half.
After four halvings, the root lies between one point two five and one point three one two five.
The interval is one sixteenth as wide as the original.
Choosing its midpoint gives an error at most half that width. More steps buy a predictable accuracy.
Now replace the curve with a jump from minus one to plus one.
The signs still differ, but there is no zero.
Continuity was the promise that made the bracket trustworthy. A sign change alone is not enough.

scenes.narration:
We want the number whose cube is two. At one, the cube is too small. At two, it is too large.

Keep a bracket with opposite signs for x cubed minus two. Because the curve is continuous, it must cross zero between them. Test the middle, one point five. Its cube is too large, so keep the left half.

The next middle is one point two five. Its cube is too small. Keep the right half. Two more tests narrow the bracket further. Each test preserves a root inside while cutting the interval width in half.

After four halvings, the root lies between one point two five and one point three one two five. The interval is one sixteenth as wide as the original. Choosing its midpoint gives an error at most half that width. More steps buy a predictable accuracy.

Now replace the curve with a jump from minus one to plus one. The signs still differ, but there is no zero. Continuity was the promise that made the bracket trustworthy. A sign change alone is not enough.
